about: Sources for /el-nino/ ('El Niño and heat in Asia') and the El Niño watch on /signals/: official ENSO bulletins, regional outlooks, national services and explainers. Each claim names the exact terms its source holds; nothing reaches a page unless the GitHub source check found every term. Bulletins keep their own issue dates and periods; unlike indices and baselines are never combined.

claims.text: NOAA CPC's discussion of 12 November 2026 keeps an El Niño Advisory: El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January–March 2027 (a greater than 79% chance), and is expected to begin weakening in early 2027. The next discussion is scheduled for 10 December 2026.

Compared with the previous month, El Niño strengthened as sea surface temperature anomalies exceeded 4.0 °C and extended farther west across the eastern equatorial Pacific; the weekly Niño-3.4 index reached +2.5 °C, and suppressed rainfall persisted over Indonesia.
NOAA puts the chance of a historic event, with a 3-month RONI of +2.5 °C or more, at about 60% for October–December and November–January.
rests_on: 60% for the October-December and November-January periods

claims.text: NOAA notes that even with a very strong El Niño, impacts consistent with El Niño are more likely but not guaranteed.

NOAA's probabilities issued in November 2026 give El Niño a 100% chance from October–December 2026 to January–March 2027, 98% for February–April, 80% for March–May and 38% for April–June 2027, when ENSO-neutral becomes most likely (61%).

NOAA verifies these probabilities with the Relative Oceanic Niño Index, defining El Niño and La Niña with ±0.5 °C thresholds in Niño-3.4 sea surface temperature departures from a 1991–2020 base period.

For March–May 2027, NOAA's strength probabilities give 53% weak, 25% moderate, 2% strong and 0% very strong; its categories rise in 0.5 °C steps, the highest being 2.0 °C or more. NOAA states that the strength of El Niño does not necessarily correspond with the strength of its influence or expected impact.
rests_on: does not necessarily correspond with the strength of the influence or expected impact

claims.text: RONI is the three-month running mean of Niño 3.4 sea surface temperature anomalies with the average tropical anomaly subtracted, rescaled to the original index's variance; its latest values are estimates that can change for up to two months.

WMO's Global Seasonal Climate Update, published 21 October 2026, forecasts the seasonal average Niño 3.4 sea surface temperature ensemble mean anomaly at about +3.8 °C for November 2026–January 2027, peaking around December, and a positive Indian Ocean Dipole declining to +0.3 °C.
rests_on: positive IOD is predicted to decline

claims.text: WMO's El Niño/La Niña Update of 3 September 2026 gave an exceptionally high likelihood of nearly 100% that El Niño persists through February 2027.

An ENSO forecast can raise or lower the likelihood of wetter, drier, warmer or cooler conditions in different regions; it does not predict with certainty that a particular drought, flood or heatwave will occur. Regional outcomes depend on the pattern of Pacific warming, the atmospheric response, timing and duration, and other climate drivers.
rests_on: does not predict with certainty that a particular drought, flood or heatwave will occur
No two El Niño events produce identical impacts

claims.text: To guide action, a climate forecast must be considered alongside exposure, vulnerability, historical impacts, sectoral knowledge and shorter-range weather information.
rests_on: considered alongside exposure, vulnerability, historical impacts, sectoral knowledge and shorter-range weather information

claims.text: The trade winds normally blow from east to west across the tropical Pacific; stronger trades push warm surface water west, deepening the warm pool and letting colder, deeper water rise in the east.
rests_on: normally blow from east to west across the tropical Pacific
The pool of warm water grows deeper
colder, deeper water to rise to the surface in the eastern half of the Pacific basin

claims.text: During El Niño, surface winds across the tropical Pacific are weaker than usual, the central and eastern Pacific are warmer than average, rainfall is below average over Indonesia, and rising air shifts to the central or eastern Pacific while sinking air increases over Indonesia.
rests_on: surface winds across the entire tropical Pacific are weaker than usual
rainfall is below average over Indonesia

claims.text: El Niño and La Niña are opposite phases of a natural pattern that swings every 3–7 years on average; scientists have low confidence in predicting exactly how a warmer world will affect ENSO.

During La Niña, cooler sea surface temperatures strengthen the trade winds and increase cold-water upwelling, reinforcing the cooling; changes in the tropical Pacific alter atmospheric circulation and can influence weather around the world.
rests_on: strengthen the trade winds and increase cold-water upwelling

claims.text: ENSO forecasts made in the northern spring are less reliable than at other times of year: a lull or valley in forecast accuracy, not a wall.
rests_on: lull or a valley in ENSO forecasting accuracy

claims.text: In Southeast Asia, El Niño typically brings drier-than-average rainfall, including for most of the Maritime Continent in September–November, raising the risk of forest fires and smoke haze; its effect is typically stronger over the southern and eastern parts of the region in June–October, and more pronounced in strong or moderate events.
rests_on: including for most of the Maritime Continent during September
stronger over the southern and eastern part of South East Asia during the months of Jun

claims.text: ASMC describes opposite rainfall, and consequently temperature, conditions during La Niña years, linking rainfall shifts to temperature in the region.

ASMC's seasonal forecast updated 5 November 2026 predicts below-normal rainfall over parts of the southeastern and northeastern Maritime Continent and southeastern Mainland Southeast Asia for November 2026–January 2027, above-normal temperature over the ASEAN region, and says national services are to be consulted for national-scale updates.
rests_on: below-normal rainfall to persist over parts of the southeastern and northeastern Maritime Continent and southeastern Mainland Southeast Asia
above-normal temperature is predicted over the ASEAN region
National Meteorological and Hydrological Services should be consulted

claims.text: Hotspots with localised smoke plumes may still occur under El Niño, particularly where below-normal rainfall is expected; the northern ASEAN dry season from the end of the year can bring more hotspot and haze activity.
rests_on: hotspots with localised smoke plumes may still occur
northern ASEAN region is expected to enter its traditional dry season

claims.text: Meteorological Service Singapore's status of 16 October 2026: the Relative Niño3.4 index was 2.1 °C for September 2026 and 1.7 °C for July–September (RONI), with the index predicted to peak during October–December 2026.
rests_on: 1.7°C for the three-month average July – September 2026

claims.text: India's Ministry of Earth Sciences (5 August 2026): El Niño has historically been associated with weaker Indian summer monsoon rainfall over parts of the country but is not the sole determinant; the Indian Ocean Dipole, the Madden-Julian Oscillation and regional ocean–atmosphere interactions also influence it. INCOIS assessed El Niño as likely to persist from June 2026 to February 2027, with probabilities of 70 to 90 per cent.
rests_on: weaker Indian Summer Monsoon rainfall over parts of the country

claims.text: Bangladesh Meteorological Department's monsoon outlook for July–September 2026 expected near-normal rainfall overall, with above-normal rainfall in the southeast, below-normal in the west and northwest, and above-normal temperature across the country.
Nepal's Department of Hydrology and Meteorology data, as reported, show eight of nine El Niño years associated with reduced monsoon rainfall, but one with above-average rainfall.
rests_on: eight of nine El Niño years were associated with reduced rainfall

claims.text: PAGASA (El Niño Advisory No. 2, 6 July 2026): El Niño increases the likelihood of below-normal rainfall, which may bring dry spells and droughts in some areas, while above-normal rainfall may still occur over the western part of the country during the southwest monsoon (Habagat).
rests_on: increases the likelihood of below-normal rainfall

claims.text: NOAA's November discussion reports a deeper-than-average thermocline in the eastern Pacific.
Warming in the central and eastern Pacific shifts the rising branch of the Walker Circulation eastward, while sinking branches shift over the Maritime Continent.
rests_on: rising branch of the Walker Circulation

claims.text: ENSO is associated with large-scale atmospheric and oceanic teleconnections.
